newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's central bank probes Nazi gold links.
newsitem.headline: Canada's central bank probes Nazi gold links.

text.p: Canada's central bank is investigating claims that it laundered more than six tons of looted Nazi gold during the Second World War, bank officials confirmed on Tuesday.

"We share your concern that the gold of other central banks held for safekeeping in Canada could have been associated in any way, however indirect, with Nazi Germany gold transactions," Bank of Canada Governor Gordon Thiessen wrote in a letter to the Canadian Jewish Congress.
"I can assure you that we will be pursuing our review quickly and thoroughly so that the situation can be clarified as soon as possible," Thiessen said in a letter written last Friday.
A U.S. intelligence document released last week said Portugal used the Swiss National Bank to swap 20 tons of looted Nazi gold for gold held in the U.S. Federal Reserve Bank and the Bank of Canada.

Other intelligence documents said that Portugal bought another two tons of gold from the Swiss through Canada and used the Bank of Canada to ship it to Sweden, Canadian Jewish Congress spokesman Bernie Farber said in a telephone interview on Tuesday.
"My guess is that there probably will be more coming," he said. "I'm not convinced there was any criminality here, but there were some very serious ethical questions."
The Bank of Canada would likely conclude its investigation in a few days, bank spokesman Bruce Yemen said.
"I guess the question would be to what extent at that time would there have been reason to wonder about a transaction of this nature," he said in a telephone interview.
Researchers at the central bank are searching for records of the transactions as well as clues about whether the Bank of Canada should have suspected Nazi links at the time.
If the investigation showed the central bank should have known better, the Canadian Jewish Congress would expect an apology, Farber said.

The U.S. document released last week said the Portuguese gold swap was made to eliminate evidence that Portugal was receiving gold stolen by the Nazis. The Allies had warned Portugal and other neutral nations they would face reprisals if they bought looted German gold.
Switzerland's central bank has denied that it laundered looted gold for Portugal during the war.
